_comment: Durable rolling journal for the Night Hawk 0DTE forensic lane. Read via `git show origin/main:docs/audit/nighthawk-0dte-live-journal.json` at the start of every firing — never trust a stale local copy. Update in place and commit+push directly to main (state file, no PR, same pattern as .blackout-agent/HEARTBEAT). Prune sessions older than ~2 trading days. Cold start on 2026-09-10 — no prior continuity existed before this file.

2026-09-10T13:46Z.note: 8 min after the 13:38 baseline. Still OPENING_DRIVE (heat 70%), still 0 committed -- roster churn is normal opening-drive noise (scores swinging +/-20pts as flow/breakout signals update minute to minute), NOT a promotion story yet since nothing has actually graduated to the ledger. 41 setups now (was 28): 4 dropped (NUAI/JOBY/BMNR/QBTS), 17 newly appeared. Biggest single mover: SPCH 66->86 (now well clear of score_floor, still WATCH, not committed -- worth checking next cycle whether it graduates or the score is itself noisy/transient).
2026-09-10T13:46Z.next_cycle_check: Did SPCH(86) or AAPL(69) finally commit? If a high-score WATCH setup sits uncommitted for multiple consecutive cycles despite clearing score_floor, that's worth a real gate-trace (what's actually blocking OPEN) rather than more roster diffing.

2026-09-10T14:08Z.note: 22 min later, heat now RTH 100%. SPCH/AAPL follow-up RESOLVED (not a finding): SPCH decayed 86->51, AAPL 69->54, both still WATCH/uncommitted -- confirms hypothesis those were transient opening-drive score noise, not a stuck gate. First 2 real commits of the session: SPCX long (score75/tierA, cortex PASS 0.72, confluence WEAK timing+VWAP-only) and SPXW short (score75/tierB, cortex PASS 0.5, confluence TRIPLE-confirmed), both committed_at_et 10:02, both trim_scale. Both look coherent at entry, no red flags. 65 WATCH setups total now.
2026-09-10T14:08Z.next_cycle_check: How are SPCX/SPXW managing? Trim triggers hit and acted on per trim_scale rules? Does SPCX's weaker confluence show up in a worse outcome than SPXW's triple-confirmed one (a single pair, not a pattern -- just an observation to track)?

2026-09-10T14:17Z.note: SPCX CLOSED: entry 3.18, mark 3.05, final pnl -4.09%, peak was only +2.2% -- never crossed the 40% trim_scale first-trigger, so no trim ever fired, CORRECT (peak too small for the rule to engage), small round-trip loss from noise-level gain, not mismanagement. SPXW still HOLD, worsening: entry 14.5, mark 8, live pnl -44.83%, peak_pnl -21.03% (never once profitable). trim_scale trim_levels correctly show fired=False on BOTH (they're GAIN triggers, irrelevant to a losing trade) -- the only loss-side protection is the flat -50% hard stop and 15:50 ET time stop, so HOLD at -44.83% is CORRECT current behavior, not a bug. This is a single in-flight loser, not a 3-instance pattern -- watching, not escalating.
2026-09-10T14:17Z.watch_next_cycle: Does SPXW's -50% stop fire correctly if it breaches, or does it round-trip back? (also: keep an eye out for the QQQ-style instant-phantom-stop shape if it DOES stop out -- this one committed at 10:02 and has been live for real elapsed time with a real gradual decay, so it does NOT look like that bug, but worth confirming the stop math is clean when/if it fires.)

2026-09-10T14:37Z.note: SPXW CLOSED, exit_pnl exactly -50.00%, closed_reason=stopped, mark 7.25 = precisely half of 14.5 entry -- clean, correctly-computed hard stop after a real ~35min gradual decay. POSITIVE confirmation: the stop mechanism itself is sound for a genuinely-decaying position (contrast with the QQQ open finding, which is specifically about a STALE ENTRY PRICE causing an instant false stop, not about the stop-math/trigger logic). Both of today's first 2 commits now closed: SPCX -4.09% (thesis), SPXW -50% (stopped) -- a rough start, nothing mechanically wrong on either. 102 WATCH setups now (normal RTH churn), 0 new commits since 10:02.

Reported to PR #4076, not fixed (touches live entry-pricing/grading logic).

open_findings.status: CONFIRMED SYSTEMIC (upgraded 2026-09-10T06:03:35Z from single-instance to 7-instance pattern via 90-day record backtest)
open_findings.summary: Near-instant (<5s of commit) 'stopped' exits at catastrophic P&L (-51% to -90%) are a recurring, mechanical, NOT-real-trade artifact, distinct from and NOT fixed by PR #4656 (which only addressed the near-zero thesis_break self-veto shape). Root cause: entry_premium falls back to stale flow_avg_fill (src/lib/zerodte/plan.ts:511-524, resolveLedgerEntryPremium) when planEntryMax is null and no fresh quote is required; CHASE_PCT's 55% no-chase guard is wider than the play's own -50% hard stop, so a 'not chasing' entry (48-54% already decayed) can already be past its own stop the instant a fresh mark is taken at commit.

confirmed_instances_stopped_lt_-10pct_wi: QQQ 2026-09-09 short score85 pnl-51.42% delta0.91s (the original single-instance find)
evidence_90d_backtest.separate_already-explained_bug_bucket: 14 more near-instant exits in [-5%,+5%] pnl band match the OTHER known shape (thesis_break, cortex narrative says BLOCKED while decision=PASS/vetoes=[]) -- all pre-date PR #4656 (16:43:45 UTC 2026-09-09), consistent with that fix, not evidence of a gap.
evidence_90d_backtest.track_record_impact: raw (as currently reported, includes both mechanical-shape buckets): n=371 valid, WR 40.4%, avg pnl -4.06%. Excluding all 24 near-instant (<5s) exits: n=347, WR 41.6%, avg pnl -3.04%. The 7-instance catastrophic-stop bucket alone drags avg P&L materially given its severity (-51% to -90% each) despite being only ~1.8% of all commits -- disproportionate weight on the headline number.

root_cause_files: src/lib/zerodte/gates.ts:1730-1736 (liveCommitPreconditionsUnmet quote_age_unknown -- didn't catch any of these 7, untraced why -- either plan.quoteAgeMs was non-null while tracking a DIFFERENT quote than the one that became entry_premium, or this precondition check isn't wired into whatever commit path FLOW/aggressor-flow-origin plays take)
evidence_ref: follow-up comment posted 2026-09-10 with the 7-instance backtest -- see PR #4076 comment thread for latest
open_findings.why_not_fixed_yet: Touches live commit/entry-pricing logic directly (resolveLedgerEntryPremium + the quote_age_unknown precondition gate). Root cause of WHY the existing guard doesn't catch this is only partially traced (haven't confirmed whether plan.quoteAgeMs was populated-but-wrong vs the precondition check being skipped entirely for this commit path) -- shipping a fix without that final trace risks making live pricing logic worse, not better. Per mandate: report with evidence and hold for direction on anything ambiguous/architecturally significant, even though v5 grants standing authority for MEASURED calibration changes -- this is a data-integrity/entry-sourcing bug, not a threshold-tuning question, so it stays in the 'hold for direction' lane.
open_findings.next_step: If greenlit: (1) finish tracing plan.quoteAgeMs propagation for a FLOW/aggressor-flow-origin commit to find exactly why quote_age_unknown didn't fire on these 7; (2) once root cause is nailed, the fix is likely either (a) require a fresh in-bound quote (not just flowAvgFill) before ANY directional commit, independent of CHASE_PCT, or (b) tighten CHASE_PCT below hard_stop_pct so a 'not chasing' entry can never already be past its own stop; (3) A/B backtest the candidate fix against this same 90-day window before shipping, same rigor as tier-exit-mode-ab.mjs.

win_loss_taxonomy.caveat: Preliminary pass only -- classification below is heuristic (peak_pnl_pct vs final pnl, score vs score_floor, cortex decision), not a full evaluateZeroDteGates replay. origin/tier metadata is NULL for most pre-August rows (schema rolled out later), so origin/tier-based win-pattern reads are only reliable for the August-onward subset -- flagged, not yet corrected for.

loss_bucket_seed.MECHANICAL_not_a_real_trade: 24 near-instant (<5s) exits -- 7 catastrophic 'stopped' (see open_findings above, NOT yet fixed) + 14 near-zero thesis_break self-veto (explained, resolved by #4656) + a few in between. EXCLUDE these from any real win/loss-pattern analysis until fixed -- they are pipeline artifacts, not trading outcomes.
loss_bucket_seed.note: Real BAD-ENTRY / BAD-EXIT / CLEAN-STOP-OUT / VARIANCE bucketing of the ~178 remaining real losses NOT yet done -- needs the same care as the mechanical-exclusion pass above (each loss needs its own entry_context read, not a bulk heuristic). Scoped as next cycle's work, not attempted this cycle given time already spent on the mechanical-pattern confirmation.

win_bucket_seed.top_quartile_winners_n31_of_127_clean_wi: score range spans 30-100 with no visible clean cutoff (matches helix-score-signal.mjs's prior finding that raw score doesn't cleanly separate outcomes for Helix -- open question whether 0DTE score has the same 'spread without order' shape, NOT yet conclusively answered here since half this sample predates tier/origin metadata rollout).
win_bucket_seed.data_quality_gap: 25 of 31 top-quartile winners (mostly July 2026) have origin=null and tier=null -- these fields didn't exist yet in entry_context at commit time for those rows. Restrict any origin/tier-based win analysis to August-onward data until this is accounted for.

score_calibration_reliability_diagram.method: 347 clean (non-mechanical) graded plays from the 90-day record, bucketed by score decile, win rate + avg pnl per bucket.
score_calibration_reliability_diagram.finding: NOT monotonic: win rate dips at 80-90 (37.9%) below both 70-80 (43.7%) and 90-101 (54.1%). This independently REPRODUCES an already-known, already-mitigated finding on record in QQQ's own tier factors ('the measured top-band inversion -- 85+ ran 33.3% WR vs 63.6% at 75-84, F-5' -- already priced in via the G-19 topBandInversionFlag / tier discount). NOT a new discovery.
score_calibration_reliability_diagram.unreconciled_discrepancy: The already-documented F-5 note says 85+ ran 33.3% WR; my 90-101 bucket here shows 54.1% WR on n=119 -- materially different number, likely different bucket boundaries (theirs is 85+, mine is 90-101, and my 80-90 bucket alone is closer at 37.9%) and/or a different/larger time window. Did NOT attempt to reconcile the exact numbers this cycle -- flagging so a future cycle (or whoever owns F-5's calibration doc) checks bucket-boundary and window differences before treating either number as final.
score_calibration_reliability_diagram.caveat: score_floor is documented as 65, yet 50 rows in this sample scored BELOW 65 (2 in 20-30, 8 in 30-40, 3 in 40-50, 15 in 50-60) and still committed -- either score_floor varies by regime/session rather than being a flat 65, or 'score' here is a later-refined value that can differ from the pre-commit gating score. Not resolved this cycle -- worth tracing before trusting the low-score buckets' small-n numbers at all.

same_session_concentration_check.method: Grouped the 90-day sample by session_date (42 of 47 sessions had 2+ commits), checked for sessions where multiple same-session commits shared direction, and separately checked a rough index/mega-cap beta cluster (SPY/QQQ/SPX/SPXW/IWM/DIA).
same_session_concentration_check.result: 14 of 42 multi-commit sessions had ALL same-session commits in the same direction; only 1 of those (2026-08-06: QQQ short -24.63%, SPXW short -50.21%) had every same-direction commit ALSO lose. Same result restricting to the beta-cluster subset: 17 sessions with 2+ cluster commits, only that same 1 instance was same-direction-and-all-loss.
same_session_concentration_check.verdict: Investigated per the mandate's evidence-first instruction (do not propose a fix before checking frequency) -- this does NOT appear to be a frequent real problem in this 90-day window (1 instance = below the standing 3+ noise threshold). NOT proposing a same-session concentration gate on this evidence. Worth a periodic re-check, not a standing watch item.
